property_summary: Only the jojoTeam address can successfully call newEmergencyOracle (non-jojoTeam callers revert).

For any caller X who is jojoTeam and any description, when X calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner equals the caller (X); the mutant that uses jojoTeam as constructor owner makes the created oracle's owner equal to jojoTeam instead, so for some callers X != jojoTeam the property is violated.

For any caller X who is jojoTeam, when X calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the emitted NewEmergencyOracle must report newOracle.owner == X (i.e., the freshly deployed EmergencyOracle's owner equals the tx sender); the mutant that uses jojoTeam as the constructor owner instead can produce a new oracle whose owner != caller for some caller X != jojoTeam.

For every caller addr (caller != jojoTeam) who is set as jojoTeam and then calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the freshly deployed EmergencyOracle's owner equals the tx sender (the caller); the mutant that uses jojoTeam as constructor owner breaks this because it sets the owner to jojoTeam instead of the caller for some caller values.

For any caller X (fuzzed) who is set as jojoTeam and then calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the address returned by the public getter for the freshly created oracle (the value of the emitted/newly stored oracle address available via the emitted event can't be read, so we instead check that creating an oracle and then calling turnOnOracle() from the same caller succeeds iff the created oracle's owner equals that caller) should allow the caller to call owner-only functions (turnOnOracle) on the newly deployed EmergencyOracle; the mutant that constructs the EmergencyOracle with jojoTeam instead of msg.sender makes the new oracle owned by jojoTeam, so for some fuzzed callers X != jojoTeam the caller will not be able to call owner-only functions — the reference always allows the creator to perform owner-only actions on its created oracle, the mutant sometimes prevents it.

For every address chosen as jojoTeam, when that address calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the deployed EmergencyOracle's owner equals jojoTeam (i.e. the contract's stored jojoTeam becomes the owner of the new oracle) — the mutant that uses msg.sender instead of jojoTeam (or vice versa) causes a mismatch for some fuzzed addresses, so observing whether the caller can successfully call an owner-only function on the freshly deployed oracle distinguishes them.

The reference contract always emits NewEmergencyOracle with the jojoTeam caller as the first (owner) field; the mutant sometimes emits the new oracle address instead, so the emitted owner field can differ from the actual caller.

For any jojoTeam caller and any description, the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first (owner) field equals the caller address in the reference contract; the mutant sometimes emits the newly deployed oracle address there instead, breaking this equality.

For every call to newEmergencyOracle by jojoTeam with any description, the reference emits an event whose first indexed address equals the caller (jojoTeam); the mutant can emit the newly deployed oracle address instead, breaking that equality for some inputs.

For every jojoTeam caller and any description, the reference emits NewEmergencyOracle whose first indexed address (owner) equals jojoTeam; the mutant sometimes emits the newly deployed oracle address there instead, so the emitted event's owner field can differ from the caller.

For every jojoTeam caller and any description, after calling newEmergencyOracle the contract's jojoTeam state variable remains equal to the caller (the function must not mutate jojoTeam); the mutant still preserves state but swaps event arguments, so instead assert that the emitted owner equals the stored jojoTeam — this holds for the reference for all inputs and the mutant will fail because it emits a different owner for some inputs (detected by comparing the logged topic of the event to jojoTeam).

For any caller address provided to newEmergencyOracle, when C is correct the function succeeds if and only if msg.sender equals jojoTeam (so calls from jojoTeam result in a NewEmergencyOracle being emitted and the newly created EmergencyOracle address is nonzero and accessible via the contract state change); the mutant that requires msg.sender == address(0) makes legitimate jojoTeam callers fail, so there exist inputs (caller == jojoTeam) for which the mutant prevents successful creation whereas the reference allows it.

For any caller address A, if A equals the contract's jojoTeam then calling newEmergencyOracle from A succeeds (creates a nonzero oracle address and emits) in the reference; the mutant that requires msg.sender==address(0) will make calls from the real jojoTeam fail, so there exist caller addresses (the jojoTeam) for which the mutant blocks creation while the reference allows it.

For any caller address X, if X equals c.jojoTeam() then calling newEmergencyOracle as X succeeds (does not revert) and thus the reference allows creation; the mutant that restricts the caller to address(0) will cause such calls by the genuine jojoTeam to revert — so the property is that calling newEmergencyOracle from the jojoTeam never reverts on the reference but can revert on the mutant.

For any address caller and any description, if the caller is set as jojoTeam then calling newEmergencyOracle(description) succeeds on the reference (does not revert) and results in a nonzero NewEmergencyOracle being created; the mutant that requires msg.sender==address(0) makes such calls from the real jojoTeam revert or fail, breaking this rule.

For every address/team and description, when the contract's jojoTeam equals a caller address, calling newEmergencyOracle(...) from that address succeeds (does not revert) on the reference; the mutant that requires msg.sender == address(0) makes such legitimate jojoTeam calls revert for at least some fuzzed jojoTeam address, breaking the rule.
